title: Triphthong Table
description: Flour-hire-coir and hvirvle-spurv-færge in one deadpan phonetics lesson. Lillith & Rubella; pronunciation guide always one vowel glide behind the melody.
stylePrompt: Educational cabaret duet at 92 BPM. Detuned upright piano (±5 cents), soft brushed snare, low-string pad. Lillith & Rubella in parallel thirds — **deadpan, never smiling**, like a 1960s language-lab film that cracked open. Lyrics showcase **English triphthongs** [aʊ̯ə̯ aɪ̯ə̯ ɔɪ̯ə̯] (flour/flower, hire/higher, coir/coyer/lawyer), plus **Danish** [iɐ̯u̯ uɐ̯u̯] (hvirvle, spurv, færge), **Spanish** [u̯ei̯ u̯ai̯] (buey, Uruguay), and rolling / r-heavy clusters (rural, ferrocarril, Børge). Diction forward in mix — consonants dry, vowels gliding. **Structural flaw:** the **pronunciation guide** (spoken IPA-ish prompts) is always **one vowel glide behind** the sung melody — the singers land the triphthong while the guide is still on the diphthong. Smash-cut optional Twilight Time handoff only if requested. Mood: Lillith & Rubella's gothic living room becomes a phonetics classroom. Runtime ~55–70 seconds. Use Lillith and Rubella voices.
lyrics:
[Intro — chalk on slate]
Tonight's lesson: three vowels in one syllable
Please keep your tongues where we can see them

[Verse 1 — Lillith]
Flour in the flower, hire in the higher
Coir in the coyer lawyer by the loir
Iron in society, sour in an hour
Player, slower — same suffix, different power

[Rubella — guide, one glide late]
(aʊ… ə) (aɪ… ə) (ɔɪ… ə)

[Verse 2 — Rubella]
Hvirvle like a spurv in a færge at sea
Børge whirls where the Danish roll free
Buey in Uruguay, cambiáis in the rain
Rolling r's on the triphthong train

[Lillith — guide, one glide late]
(iɐ… u) (uɐ… u) (u̯ei… u̯ai)

[Chorus — duet, parallel thirds]
Triphthong table, set for three
Glide on glide on glide for me
Flour-hire-coir in one breath — don't blink
Society's iron sour on the brink
That's phonetics for us

[Bridge — spoken fast, both]
Rural juror, ferrocarril, corroboratory corrobori
W Szczebrzeszynie chrząszcz brzmi w trzcinie — we don't ask you to spell it
Strč prst skrz krk — we only ask you to feel it

[Outro — button line]
That's phonetics for us
(the guide finishes the first vowel of the last word after the song ends)
notes:
## Phonetic research basis
- **English triphthongs (RP / non-rhotic):** [aʊ̯ə̯] flour vs disyllabic flower; [aɪ̯ə̯] hire vs higher; [ɔɪ̯ə̯] coir vs coyer/lawyer/loir; also society, iron, sour, player, slower (Wells *Accents of English*).
- **Danish triphthongs:** [iɐ̯u̯] hvirvle 'whirl'; [uɐ̯u̯] spurv 'sparrow'; [ɛɐ̯u̯] færge 'ferry'; [œ̞ɐ̯u̯] Børge.
- **Spanish triphthongs:** [u̯ei̯] buey; [u̯ai̯] Uruguay; [i̯ai̯]/[i̯ei̯] cambiáis / cambiéis (European Spanish).
- **Shibboleth / cluster garnish:** Polish *W Szczebrzeszynie chrząszcz brzmi w trzcinie*; Czech *strč prst skrz krk*; rural juror (legal tongue-twister meme); ferrocarril (Spanish rolling r).
